recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — give the definition with its quantifier, and say what your example has to be checked against.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words for every a ∈ A carry the definition. One missing pair (a, a) is enough to make the relation not reflexive, so the condition must be stated for all of A.
lines: Let R be a relation on a set A, that is R ⊆ A × A.
(a, a) ∈ R  for every a ∈ A
So every element of A must be related to itself.

recall.must_convey: That R on A is reflexive when (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A.
accept: a comma a is in R for every a in A
every element is related to itself
all the pairs a a must be in the relation
prathi element tanaki tanu related ga undali
reflexive means a R a holds for all a

steps.why: Reflexive is a condition on all of A, not on part of it, so the quantifier is the part being marked. A definition that says some a instead of every a describes a different and much weaker property.
steps.memory_tip: Reflexive means every element is related to itself — look for the full list (1,1), (2,2), (3,3).
common_mistakes: Writing (a, a) ∈ R for some a ∈ A, which is a far weaker condition.
Writing a R b ⇒ b R a, which is symmetric, not reflexive.
Stating the condition without saying R is a relation on one set A.

steps.label: Check it on an example
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Check the elements of A one at a time. The extra pair (1, 3) is allowed — a reflexive relation may hold more pairs than the (a, a) ones.
lines: Check each element of A in turn:
1 gives (1, 1) ∈ R,   2 gives (2, 2) ∈ R,   3 gives (3, 3) ∈ R

lines.text: ∴ R is a reflexive relation on A.

recall.must_convey: That every element of A is checked and its (a, a) pair is found in R, so R is reflexive.
accept: one one two two and three three are all in R so it is reflexive
check every element of A one by one
the extra pair one three does not stop it being reflexive
moodu elements ki kuda a a pairs unnayi kabatti reflexive
all three self pairs are present

steps.why: The example shows the definition asks only for the pairs (a, a) to be present. Nothing is said about the other pairs, so (1, 3) sitting in R does not affect the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Read down the elements of A, not down the list of pairs — a missing element is easier to see that way.
common_mistakes: Thinking (1, 3) must be matched by (3, 1) before R can be reflexive.
Checking two elements of A and stopping before the third.
Calling R reflexive when it holds (1, 1) and (2, 2) but the set A also contains 3.
